Pause Delinquency Pause Delinquency is a delinquency management enhancement that allows an authorized user to pause or freeze the delinquency calculation for a loan for a defined period. The feature affects both loan‑level delinquency assessment and installment‑level delinquency classification, and it is implemented as a loan‑level control that can be activated and later resumed. When paused, the system refrains from reclassifying delinquency buckets during the pause window, while payments made on delinquent amounts may still resolve the delinquent state. The pause state is represented by a loan‑level flag and an effective pause period, and changes to this flag emit domain events. The design is scoped to loan‑level delinquency control and its impact on the installment delinquency process. It is not a product level setting and does not alter the underlying delinquency bucket definitions themselves. The pause mechanism is governed by the lifecycle of delinquency actions stored against a loan, and the system exposes an API surface to view and create these actions. The daily COB (close of business) processing will re‑evaluate delinquency buckets when pauses are not active, and it will respect the current pause state when computing delinquency for each loan. Key concepts and guarantees The pause state is represented by actions stored in a dedicated data structure (the delinquency action history) and a boolean indicator exposed through loan read endpoints. A loan is considered paused if the current business date falls inside an active pause window. The pause window is defined by a start date and an optional end date. A valid pause must start today or later and must last at least one day (start date strictly precedes end date). Resume actions restore delinquency calculation. A resume action has a start date (which is the effective date of resumption) and must not specify an end date. Pause and resume actions are persisted as discrete entries against the loan, and overlapping pauses are not allowed by validation rules. When the pause flag changes, events are emitted to reflect the new state. The system also extends collection data with a delinquency paused flag so external consumers can observe current pause status. Execution lifecycle and state transitions The pause state is fundamentally a binary condition: Active (delinquency calculation enabled) and Paused (delinquency calculation disabled). The following state transitions are evidenced by the design and related implementation points: Active to Paused: A Pause action is created for an active loan and the pause period includes the current business date. Paused to Active: A Resume action is created to end the pause; delinquency calculation resumes from the start date of the resume action. Attempts to pause while already paused are validated as invalid at the API boundary (overlapping pauses are not permitted). Mermaid diagram (simplified): mermaidstateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Active Active --> Paused : pause action Paused --> Active : resume action Data model and persistence A dedicated table stores delinquency actions associated with each loan. The table captures the action type, effective window, and audit information: Table: m_loan_delinquency_action id: BIGINT, PK, not null loan_id: BIGINT, index, not null action: VARCHAR(128), not null (e.g., PAUSE, RESUME) start_date: Date, not null end_date: Date, optional created_by: BIGINT, not null created_on_utc: timestamp, not null last_modified_by: BIGINT, not null last_modified_on_utc: timestamp, not null Algorithm to determine whether delinquency calculation is paused for a loan The database layer provides the following decision logic (as specified in the design): If no record is found for the loan, delinquency calculation is enabled (not paused). If a PAUSE entry is returned by the query, delinquency calculation is paused. If a RESUME entry is returned, delinquency calculation is enabled. The exact query used to determine the paused state is: Pause state query () Query: SELECT * FROM m_loan_delinquency_action WHERE ((action = "pause" AND end_date is not null AND :business_date >= start_date AND :business_date <= end_date) OR (action = "resume" AND end_date is null AND :business_date >= start_date)) AND loan_id = :loan_id ORDERY BY created_on_utc DESC LIMIT 1;]]

Where business_date represents the current processing date used by the delinquency computation. The presence of a PAUSE entry in effect on the business date indicates that the delinquency calculation is paused; the presence of a RESUME entry indicates that the calculation is enabled again. If the query returns no rows, the delinquency calculation is considered enabled.

API design and endpoints

The feature exposes endpoints to view and create delinquency actions for a loan. The interaction model is as follows: 1. Retrieve all delinquency actions for a loan
  • HTTP method and path:
  • GET /loans/{loanid}/delinquency-actions
  • GET /loans/external-id/{loanExternalId}/delinquency-actions
  • Response body (example):
Actions[{"id":"123","action":"pause","startDate":"2023-10-05","endDate":"2023-10-08","created_by":"","created_on_utc":"","last_modified_by":"","last_modified_on_utc":""},...]
2. Create a new delinquency action for a loan
  • HTTP method and path:
  • POST /loans/{loanid}/delinquency-actions
  • POST /loans/external-id/{loanExternalId}/delinquency-actions
  • Request body (example):
json
